title: The Departed
tagline: Two rats. One city. Plenty of chowder.
about: A cop goes undercover with Boston's Irish mob while a mob mole rises in the police.
cue: Serve the mains when Costigan and Sullivan both graduate from the academy.
faces: Up the block. Everybody knows everybody.

Oyster crackers.Cops or crooks, same chowder.How to make it150g bacon, diced1 brown onion, diced2 celery sticks, diced400g potatoes, diced500ml clam juice or fish stock2 sprigs of thyme250g chopped clam meat200ml thickened cream100g oyster crackersDice the bacon, onion, celery and potatoes.Fry the bacon until crisp, then sweat the onion and celery in the fat until soft.Add the potatoes, clam juice and thyme and simmer until the potato is tender.Stir in the clam meat and cream and warm through. Serve in cups with oyster crackers.Soda bread and butterBaked here each morning, cut thick, salted butter.Start at the bar.How to make it250g wholemeal flour250g plain flour1 tsp bicarbonate of soda1 tsp salt450ml buttermilk100g salted butterMix the flours, bicarb and salt, then stir in the buttermilk to a soft dough. Shape into a round and cut a deep cross on top.Bake at 220°C until golden and it sounds hollow when tapped underneath.Rest the loaf, then slice thick and serve with the salted butter.MainsAcademy fish and chipsWhite fish in lager batter, chips, minted mushy peas, malt vinegar.The Staties, cops' side.How to make it200g plain flour, for batter50g cornflour330ml ice-cold lager800g flathead fillets50g plain flour, for dusting1kg potatoes, cut into chips400g frozen peas20g butter1 bunch mint2 L vegetable oil, for frying2 tbsp malt vinegarsalt, to tasteCut the potatoes into chips, rinse and dry well. Whisk the batter flour, cornflour and cold lager together.Fry the chips in oil at 140°C until pale and soft, then drain.Cook the peas, then crush with the butter and chopped mint and keep warm.Dust the fish in flour, dip in batter and fry at 180°C in batches until golden and crisp.Fry the chips again at 185°C until crisp. Salt well and serve with the fish, peas and malt vinegar.SweetsBoston cream pieSponge, vanilla custard, dark chocolate ganache.The Crew side. Nobody talks.How to make it7 eggs180g caster sugar120g plain flour300ml full cream milk25g cornflour100g dark chocolate100ml thickened creamWhisk 4 of the eggs with half the sugar until thick and pale. Fold in the flour and divide between two lined 20cm tins.Bake at 180°C until springy, then turn out and cool completely.Heat the milk. Whisk 3 yolks with the remaining sugar and cornflour, whisk in the hot milk, return to the pan and stir until thick.Chill the custard until cold and set.Sandwich the sponges with custard. Melt the chocolate with the cream and pour over the top.DrinksCostigan's cranberryCranberry juice, fresh lime, orange, soda, crushed ice. Vodka on request.Cleans you out.How to make it400ml cranberry juice60ml lime juice60ml orange juice20ml sugar syrup200ml soda water4 cups crushed ice4 lime wedges120ml vodka, optional (30ml per glass)Juice the limes and orange.Shake the cranberry juice, lime juice, orange juice and syrup with ice, then strain into 4 short glasses of crushed ice. Top with soda and a lime wedge. Add vodka first for the grown-up version.
